source: Zhou et al. (2024) Metacognitive Retrieval-Augmented LLMs (MetaRAG)
finding: Monitor-evaluate-plan loop for multi-hop QA. Monitoring decides whether to trigger evaluation; evaluation names why the answer falls short; planning repairs it. Beat Reflexion and other RAG baselines.
numbers: HotpotQA EM/F1: MetaRAG 37.8/49.9 vs Reflexion 30.0/43.4, IR-CoT 31.4/40.3, CoT 22.4/34.2. 2WikiMultihopQA EM/F1: MetaRAG 42.8/50.8 vs Reflexion 31.8/41.7, IR-CoT 30.8/42.6. Text states gains of 26.0% and 34.6% over baseline.
limits: Uses an LLM critic; monitor signal partly model-judged. Two multi-hop QA sets only; ablation on 100 sampled HotpotQA questions.
agent_relevance: Direct use of Brown-style plan/monitor/evaluate as an agent loop; shows a gated evaluate step beats always-reflect. Fits S6 trigger.

source: Elenjical, Kavuri, Varma (2026) Think2: Grounded Metacognitive Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Prompt that forces Ann Brown's Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation phases. On a non-reasoning 8B model it HURT accuracy; on a native reasoning model it was top or runner-up.
numbers: Llama-3-8B GSM8K: Standard 80.71, CoT 77.98, Ann Brown 69.55. CRUXEval-O: CoT 25.62 vs Ann Brown 5.12. CorrectBench: Std 52.91 vs Ann Brown 68.14. Qwen-3-8B GSM8K 91.65 (Std 91.72); AIME 5.89 vs 4.82 Std. Overall error rate 4.1% vs 7.4% baselines (McNemar p=0.0005), but not significant vs CoT alone (p>0.05).
limits: Two 8B models, greedy decoding, small absolute AIME numbers; code not yet released; preprint. | CORRECTION (Think2 PDF opened): CorrectBench Llama-3-8B is Std 52.91, CoT 75.02, Ann Brown 68.14. Ann Brown beats Standard but LOSES to plain CoT. CRUXEval-O Std is 5.25, so Ann Brown 5.12 equals Standard; CoT 25.62 is the outlier.
agent_relevance: Uniform forced regulation costs accuracy on weaker models: supports G1 (signal-triggered, not scheduled). Regulation helps when the task is diagnosis.

source: Elenjical et al. (2026) Think2, self-correction funnel and human study
finding: Self-correction funnel on error cases: models often know an error may exist but cannot diagnose it. Structured monitoring raised correct diagnosis and recovery. 580 blinded human pairs favoured the metacognitive traces.
numbers: Aggregate baselines: explicit awareness 51.2%, correct diagnosis 27.9%, successful improvement 16.3%. Ann Brown: diagnosis 58.3%, improved 50.0% (CoT 25.0%). Human win rate vs all: trust 84.1%, self-awareness 84.2%, deployable 80.0%.
limits: Funnel based on small counts (e.g. 12 of 24 cases). Humans rated trace style, which can reflect verbosity not competence; authors note this risk.
agent_relevance: Awareness without diagnosis is the gap: add code-located failing output (G2) rather than asking the model to self-diagnose.

source: Dong et al. (2025) Meta-R1: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Metacognition
finding: Cascaded meta-level model (small, 1.5B-3B) does proactive planning, online regulation and early stopping over an object-level reasoning model.
numbers: Up to +27.3% over SOTA baselines on 3 benchmarks; tokens cut to 15.7%-32.7% of vanilla (average reduction 24.2%-32.7% in text); efficiency up to +14.8%; MATH500 with R1-Distill-Qwen-32B +5.3%. Scaling the meta model 3B to 14B gave only +0.1 for 14-19% more tokens.
limits: Preprint; baselines are 8 methods chosen by authors; difficulty rating by small models.
agent_relevance: Separate small controller for plan, monitor, stop is a working template for the program-decides rule; the controller need not be large.

source: Huang et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without oracle labels, asking the model to review and fix its answer does not help and often hurts. With oracle stopping the gains look large, which explains earlier optimistic papers.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 75.1 (round 1) -> 74.7 (round 2); CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8; HotpotQA 26.0 -> 25.0. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0. With oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 95.5; HotpotQA 26.0 -> 49.0. 74.7% of GSM8K answers unchanged; changes go correct-to-wrong more than the reverse.
limits: Tested GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Llama-2 with fixed prompts; later reasoning models behave differently (see c13, c15).
agent_relevance: Core support for G2/G3: a review step with no external signal is a coin flip with downside. Never let the model decide to stop on its own opinion.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Agent keeps a text memory of reflections on failed trials and retries. Large gains where an external success signal exists (unit tests, environment reward).
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion completed 130 of 134 tasks; +22% absolute over baselines; HotPotQA +20%; HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%. ReAct-only stalled between trials 6 and 7.
limits: Success signal came from ground truth or tests, so it is not intrinsic self-evaluation (Huang 2024, Kamoi 2024). Failure mode named: agent believes it holds an item it does not.
agent_relevance: The reflect-after-failure loop is an LLM version of 'Is it getting me anywhere?', but only valid with a real check. Matches S6 trigger on failed test.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: Same model generates, critiques, and rewrites. Big gains on style and preference tasks; smaller on code.
numbers: About 20% absolute average gain over one-step generation; 5-40% absolute on preference tasks for GPT-3.5/ChatGPT/GPT-4; up to 13% on code; Code Optimization +8.7 absolute for GPT-4. Failure analysis: introducing a new problem (20%), ignoring feedback (25%).
limits: Many tasks lack a ground truth; Huang 2024 shows reasoning tasks do not share the gain. Evaluation partly by model or human preference.
agent_relevance: Self-feedback fits open-ended quality, not reasoning checks. Keep out of answer-correctness steps.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Splits self-correction into finding the mistake and fixing it. Finding is the bottleneck. With the true mistake location given, correction works.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake: 2186 CoT traces over 5 tasks. Best model GPT-4 reaches 52.87 overall mistake-finding accuracy (direct step prompting). Backtracking with oracle location: multistep arithmetic +43.92 on wrong traces, -6.67 on right traces; tracking shuffled objects +23.53 / -11.11. Random location gives smaller gains (+11.76 / -15.56).
limits: Mistake sets from PaLM 2 traces, 2023 models, 300 traces per task for backtracking; oracle labels not available at run time.
agent_relevance: Strongest support for G2: code locates the error, the model fixes it. Splits monitor from control as Nelson and Narens do.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: Survey of self-correction papers. Finds no prior work showing successful self-correction from prompted-LLM feedback on general tasks. Works with reliable external feedback and with large-scale fine-tuning.
numbers: Three headline claims: (1) no demonstrated prompted self-correction in general tasks except tasks exceptionally suited; (2) works with external feedback (code interpreter, search); (3) fine-tuning at scale enables it. Bottleneck named as feedback generation.
limits: Literature to May 2024; reasoning-model era not covered; some positive results are task-specific.
agent_relevance: Treat prompted self-review as unproven; invest in code-side feedback. Gives a checklist for fair experiments to reuse in our own tests.

source: Wang and Zhao (2024) Metacognitive Prompting Improves Understanding in LLMs
finding: Five-stage prompt (understand, judge, evaluate, decide, confidence) modelled on human metacognition. Small consistent gains on NLU tasks, no tools.
numbers: GPT-4 zero-shot, ten NLU sets: MP beats CoT and plan-and-solve on all; e.g. 89.9/86.2 vs CoT 88.9/84.7 and PS 89.4/85.3 on the first set; 43.8 vs CoT 37.4 and PS 39.6 on another. Average gains over CoT reported as roughly 4.8% to 6.4% across models.
limits: NLU classification tasks, not multi-step reasoning; gains small on strong models; Think2 found MP below CoT on some tasks for 8B models.
agent_relevance: Self-questioning prompts give modest gains on comprehension but are weak evidence for reasoning scaffolds.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting
finding: Planning before solving as a zero-shot prompt. Reduces missing-step errors versus zero-shot CoT. A prompt-level analogue of the planning half of regulation.
numbers: text-davinci-003 arithmetic average over 6 sets: CoT 70.4, PS 73.5, PS+ 76.7. GSM8K: CoT 56.4, PS 57.0, PS+ 59.3. MultiArith 83.8 -> 92.2 (PS).
limits: Small GSM8K gain (about +3 with PS+); older base model; effect much smaller on modern reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Planning alone is a weak lever on GSM8K-level problems; value likely shows when the plan is checked by code.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) Training Language Models to Self-Correct via RL (SCoRe)
finding: Multi-turn RL on self-generated traces teaches intrinsic self-correction. Base models and standard SFT make the second attempt worse.
numbers: Gemini base on MATH: accuracy@t1 52.6%, @t2 41.4%, change -11.2 points; correct-to-incorrect 15.8% vs incorrect-to-correct 4.6%. SCoRe: +15.6% absolute self-correction gain on MATH, +9.1% on HumanEval.
limits: Needs training; our scaffold cannot train. Gemini 1.0/1.5 family only.
agent_relevance: Confirms prompting alone leaves a negative second-attempt effect; learned regulation requires training we are not doing, so use code gating.

source: Tsui (2025, COLM 2026) Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot
finding: Models fix an error when it is shown as coming from the user but not when it sits in their own output. Appending the word 'Wait' reactivates correction.
numbers: 14 open non-reasoning models: average blind spot 64.5%. Appending 'Wait' cut it by 89.3% and raised mean accuracy by 156%. Fine-tuning on 5,306 error-correction traces (2 epochs LoRA) cut it 76.0%. Cause traced to SFT data with near-zero correction sequences.
limits: Mostly synthetic injected errors; non-reasoning models; steering analysis on two model families only.
agent_relevance: Cheap trigger: present a past error as a separate input or add a correction marker at S6. Fits G2 (cite the real failing output).

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling (budget forcing)
finding: Budget forcing: suppress end-of-thinking or append 'Wait' to make the model keep checking, or cut thinking to stop early. Accuracy grows with forced thinking time.
numbers: s1-32B trained on 1,000 examples; AIME24 about 50% to 57% as test-time compute scaled (Table 3: 50.0 with 1K data, 57.6 with budget forcing). Forcing caps near 30,000 thinking tokens and lets the model answer when stuck in a loop.
limits: Gains saturate; forcing more thinking also loops. Math only (AIME24, MATH500, GPQA). | CORRECTION (s1 PDF opened): 57.6 is GPQA Diamond of the s1K ablation, not AIME24. AIME24 is 50.0 without budget forcing and 56.7 with scaling (paper abstract: 50% to 57%).
agent_relevance: Code-set budget and forced re-check are a program-controlled regulation mechanism; matches 'program keeps the budget'.

source: Chen et al. (2025) On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models spend large compute on easy questions. Later solutions rarely change the answer. Efficiency metrics plus self-training reduce tokens with accuracy kept.
numbers: For 'what is 2 plus 3?' o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. In more than 92% of cases the first solution round was already correct; first round is under 60% of tokens (QwQ on ASDIV: 287 tokens, 38.7% of the response).
limits: Open models QwQ-32B-Preview and R1 variants; fix needs self-training.
agent_relevance: Failure of the 'am I done?' monitor: models do not stop when ahead. Argues for code-side stop rules on agreement or check pass.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Opposite failure: models switch strategy too often and abandon promising paths. Incorrect answers show more thought switches. A decoding penalty on switch tokens (TIP) improves accuracy without tuning.
numbers: AIME2024: incorrect responses have more thoughts than correct ones (figure shows e.g. 26.4 vs 12.6 for one model) and longer length. TIP raised accuracy on QwQ-32B-Preview and R1-Distill-Qwen-32B across the three test sets; a prompt instruction alone gave only modest change.
limits: Exact per-dataset TIP numbers not cleanly extracted from the table here; open models, math only.
agent_relevance: Switch-too-early and stop-too-late both occur. Supports G1 (change strategy only on a signal) and a code-side minimum-depth rule before switching operators.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs
finding: GPT-4 as verifier of its own answers in Game of 24, graph colouring and STRIPS planning gives false positives and false negatives, so a self-critique loop degrades. A sound external verifier makes the loop work.
numbers: 100 instances per domain. With a sound verifier plus LLM critique, graph colouring reaches near 40%. One verification-accuracy example rises from 87.0% (3567/4100) to 98.8% (4051/4100) with CoT but still not enough for sound loops.
limits: GPT-4 only; formal tasks; critique quality varies by domain.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for G3/G5: verification must be code-checkable; an LLM judge of its own plan is unsound.

source: Stechly, Marquez, Kambhampati (2023) GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong
finding: In graph colouring, the content of the critique barely matters. Binary 'wrong' feedback, one error, or all errors give similar results; random sampling matches.
numbers: With a sound verifier, about 40% correct. Differences between feedback types insignificant. Sampling n=15 at t=1.0 also reaches 40%: blindfolded guessing does just as well as careful, crafted feedback.
limits: One domain (graph colouring) with GPT-4; critique may be better in other domains.
agent_relevance: The gain from reflect loops can be just resampling. Compare against best-of-N before crediting reflection.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the Planning Abilities of LLMs: A Critical Investigation
finding: Blocksworld planning: GPT-4 solves about a third of instances. Renaming predicates (Mystery Blocksworld) collapses it, so it is retrieval-like, not planning.
numbers: GPT-4 about 34% on Blocksworld (210 of 600 zero-shot natural language). Mystery Blocksworld: 1 of 600 solved; randomized mystery 0. PDDL prompt: 106 solved on Blocksworld, 3 on the obfuscated version.
limits: GPT-4 and earlier GPT models, before reasoning models; o1-class models score much higher in later work.
agent_relevance: Planning in the model is weak without a planner or verifier. Our plan step should be checked by code, as in LLM-Modulo.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
finding: Position paper: LLM generates candidate plans; external critics (model-based verifiers) check and send back; argued to beat autonomous LLM planning and self-critique.
numbers: Argues from the Valmeekam and Stechly results above. No new headline metric taken from this paper.
limits: Position paper; later empirical LLM-Modulo results not read.
agent_relevance: Architecture parallel to our schema: model fills the slot, program critics decide transitions.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 labels math questions with skills; using skill labels and skill-exemplars as in-context examples improves solving.
numbers: 11.6% enhancement over CoT on MATH (GPT-4); 7.52% improvement over PAL baseline on MATH code solutions; skills from a strong LLM also help weaker LLMs.
limits: Labels and exemplars come from the same dataset family; transfer to other sets partial.
agent_relevance: A cheap 'what kind of problem is this' monitor step that can be stored as conditional knowledge in the class record.

source: Synthesis of the sources above: where intrinsic regulation works for LLMs
finding: Pattern across studies: regulation helps when (a) an outside check supplies the failure signal (Reflexion, MetaRAG, oracle in Huang), (b) the error is shown as external input (Tsui), (c) a trained or separate controller is used (SCoRe, Meta-R1). Plain prompted self-review is flat or negative (Huang, Tyen, Stechly).
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.9 -> 74.7 intrinsic vs 95.5 oracle (Huang); mistake finding 52.87 best (Tyen); Think2 funnel 16.3% -> 50.0% only with forced phases.
limits: This line is the agent's synthesis, not a new study; inputs were all read. | CORRECTION: 95.5 is GPT-4 standard-prompt GSM8K, NOT an oracle figure. Oracle GSM8K: GPT-3.5 84.3 (from 75.9), GPT-4 97.5 (from 95.5).
agent_relevance: Design rule for S6: the trigger and the error location must come from code; the model may only repair.

source: Synthesis: effect differs between non-reasoning and reasoning models (Think2 and Tsui)
finding: Forced metacognitive structure hurts a standard 8B model but is neutral to helpful for a reasoning-native model. Reasoning-model training data contain far more correction sequences than SFT data.
numbers: Llama-3-8B GSM8K 80.71 -> 69.55 with Ann Brown; Qwen-3-8B 91.72 -> 91.65 (flat). Tsui: SFT sets have near-zero correction sequences.
limits: Compiled across two papers; different models and tasks.
agent_relevance: Whether a regulatory scaffold helps depends on the base model; test on the target model before adopting.

source: Synthesis: Reflexion limits and what the Huang critique implies
finding: Reflexion gains on ALFWorld and HumanEval rely on an external signal (environment success, unit tests). Huang 2024 and Kamoi 2024 flag this as not intrinsic self-correction.
numbers: ALFWorld 130/134 and HumanEval 91% with signal. Huang oracle vs intrinsic on GSM8K GPT-3.5: 95.5 vs 74.7.
limits: Compilation; Reflexion authors do not claim intrinsic correction. | CORRECTION: same as c22. GPT-3.5 oracle GSM8K is 84.3, not 95.5.
agent_relevance: Progress monitoring should be written as code checks (tests, state diff), not prompts.

source: Synthesis: cost of regulation (tokens vs gains)
finding: Regulation costs compute; a small controller can cut it. Meta-R1: 3B meta model is the best trade; Chen: first round correct in over 92% of cases; Wang: wrong answers switch more.
numbers: Meta-R1 token use 15.7%-32.7% of vanilla; 14B meta adds +0.1 for 18.6% more tokens.
limits: Compiled across three papers; different models.
agent_relevance: S6 should be rare and cheap: gate by disagreement or failed check, and keep the controller small.

source: Gap statement: no head-to-head of the human self-question 'Is it getting me anywhere?' in LLM agents
finding: In the sources read this session, no study tests the exact human self-question as a stop-or-switch prompt against a code-based progress counter. Closest are Think2 monitoring phase and the TIP/overthinking papers.
numbers: None measured; gap statement. Search limited to arXiv and one web search; not exhaustive.
limits: Absence of evidence in a limited search, not proof of absence. | Gap kept. Still true after cross-check.
agent_relevance: Run our own test: self-question prompt vs code progress rule at S6, per the SUBFIELDS research question.
